title: Lowest Common Ancestor of Deepest Leaves
statement:
Given the root of a binary tree, return the lowest common ancestor of its deepest leaves.

Recall that the depth of a node is the number of edges in the path from the root to the node. The deepest leaves are the nodes with the highest depth.
The LCA of the deepest leaves is a node that is the ancestor of all the deepest leaves and has the highest depth.
constraints:
1 <= The number of nodes in the tree <= 1000
0 <= Node.val <= 1000
inputFormat: A single line containing space-separated strings mapping the level-order traversal of the tree.
outputFormat: Print the level-order mapping of the subtree rooted at the LCA of the deepest leaves.

examples.explanation: Deepest leaves are 7 and 4. Their LCA is 2. The subtree rooted at 2 is 2, 7, 4.
The root is the only node.
